BBC 23 Nov 16:54

Westminster setting NI budget would be massive overreach - O'Neill

Michelle O'Neill said that \"everything we are doing is about trying to prioritise a budget\"

Michelle O'Neill has long blonde hair and is wearing a cream checked blazer and white shirt.

The government setting Stormont's budget would be a \"massive overreach\", Northern Ireland's First Minister Michelle O'Neill has said.

She described the prospect as a \"dangerous precedent\" and said the power-sharing executive would continue pressing Westminster for \"fairer funding\".

The Sinn Féin vice-president said she had asked Deputy First Minister Emma Little-Pengelly to join her in seeking \"direct engagement\" with Prime Minister Andy Burnham on the budget stalemate.

Democratic Unionist Party (DUP) leader Gavin Robinson said he had already spoken to the prime minister \"weeks ago\" and engagements involving O'Neill \"can't be business as usual\" following the Drumcree parading dispute.

No budget has been agreed by the Northern Ireland Executive more than seven months into the financial year.

With no agreed plan, public services have been operating under contingency arrangements – allowing departments to spend up to 95% of last year's funding.

Secretary of State Sir Chris Bryant has repeatedly said there is \"no more money\"

Secretary of State Sir Chris Bryant has repeatedly said there is \"no more money\" after offering an extra £1.5bn over the next three years in a bid to resolve the budget deadlock.

But Stormont ministers have insisted the funding offer does not go far enough to allow them to agree a financial plan.

In the Northern Ireland Assembly on Monday, the first minister addressed the prospect of the government striking a budget in the absence of executive agreement.

O'Neill said that \"everything we are doing is about trying to prioritise a budget\".

\"If the British government were to step in to do a budget over our heads, that would be a massive overreach,\" she said.

\"It would be a constitutional overreach. It would be a very dangerous precedent also for them to set.

\"So instead of the megaphone diplomacy from this secretary of state, they should actually get behind all of us in actually demanding fairer funding.\"

The first minister said it was \"not a case of refusing to set a budget\" but instead about \"fighting for a better budget\".

\"Today I have asked the deputy first minister to join with me in asking for a direct engagement with Andy Burnham,\" she added.

'Dereliction of responsibility'

O'Neill said it would be a \"dereliction of responsibility\" if the DUP minister refused, adding: \"I want us to have that conversation because I want us to get a budget.\"

However the DUP leader said he had already spoken to the prime minister \"two weeks ago about these issues\".

\"So we've been engaging in those discussions continually,\" he told reporters earlier at Stormont.

\"You know that whenever you take your seat in Westminster you get the opportunity to represent the people where it matters most.\"

He appeared to reject the first minister's suggestion of jointly seeking engagement with the prime minister due to the Drumcree parading dispute.

DUP Gavin Robinson leader said he had already spoken to the prime minister \"two weeks ago about these issues\"

Last month the DUP, which shares power with Sinn Féin in the four-party executive, announced it would block official engagements involving O'Neill in response to the fall-out.

Robinson said that \"the prime minister knows, and you all know too, that it can't be business as usual\".

\"We are not prepared to allow this first minister to carry on as if things were as they always had been,\" he said.

\"That's a political problem she has, but it's not going to harm the people in Northern Ireland because it hasn't held us back from the engagement that we've already had.\"

O'Neill's comments in the assembly chamber were in response to Matthew O'Toole of the Social Democratic and Labour Party (SDLP).

The assembly member, who leads the official opposition at Stormont, said it would be a \"profound failure\" and an \"undermining of devolution\" if the government ended up setting a budget.

\"But that will happen if the executive refuses to set one, because if it doesn't happen this place will run out of cash,\" he said.

O'Toole added that for Irish nationalists, Westminster setting a budget would \"undermine our case for taking responsibility into our own hands here\".

Read more on the debate about the UK and the European Union

Neon signs made for Stanley Kubrick's Eyes Wide Shut film were among the props that went under the hammer in south-west London last week.

God's Own Junk Yard also had pieces made for Tomb Raider, Bridget Jones's Diary and Elton John for sale on Thursday at its workshop on Lots Road, Fulham.

Matthew Bracey, from the family-run business, says materials used to make traditional neon are becoming harder to find as LEDs take over.

He believes neon could be worth more than gold in 10 years' time.
